source_caption:
🎬 Claws (2017–2022)

Claws follows Desna Simms, a determined and ambitious nail salon owner working in Manatee County, Florida, who dreams of escaping her difficult circumstances and building a better future for herself and the women around her. Running the Nail Artisans salon alongside her loyal but unpredictable group of employees, Desna struggles to balance her business responsibilities, personal relationships, and the demands of caring for her autistic brother, Dean. However, beneath the salon’s glamorous appearance lies a dangerous connection to organized crime, as Desna and her coworkers become involved in a money-laundering operation controlled by ruthless criminals. What begins as an opportunity to earn extra money quickly spirals into a chaotic world of betrayal, violence, dangerous alliances, and unexpected power struggles. Alongside her closest friends, including the outspoken Jennifer, mysterious Quiet Ann, glamorous Polly, and ambitious Virginia, Desna must navigate complicated relationships, criminal threats, and shocking secrets while fighting to protect her business and loved ones. From outrageous confrontations and hilarious misunderstandings to deadly rivalries and emotional revelations, the women discover that achieving independence comes with unexpected consequences. Combining dark comedy, gripping crime drama, unforgettable characters, and unpredictable twists, the series explores friendship, loyalty, ambition, survival, empowerment, and the dangerous pursuit of success.

🎭 Genre: Crime • Comedy-Drama • Dark Comedy

⭐ IMDb: 7.4/10

⏱️ Runtime: 45–60 minutes per episode • TV-MA

🎥 Creator: Eliot Laurence

📺 Where to Watch: Check Hulu, Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV, and Fandango at Home for current streaming or digital purchase availability. Availability varies by region.

source_details.synopsis: Claws is an American comedy-drama television series created by Eliot Laurence that aired on TNT from June 11, 2017, to February 6, 2022. Set in Palmetto, Florida, the series is mostly filmed in New Orleans. The series was ordered for a first season containing 10 episodes on December 13, 2016, and was originally developed as a half-hour, single-camera comedy for HBO. Three more ten-episode seasons followed, in 2017, 2018 and 2021.
